thread.title: Top Stock Gainers: Visa, Goldman, Apple Power Dow Higher | Investor's Business Daily

author: KEN SHREVE
title: Top Stock Gainers: Visa, Goldman, Apple Power Dow Higher | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market held solid gains in late-afternoon trading Wednesday after a bullish performance Tuesday. Top stock gainers in the Dow Jones included Visa ( V ), Goldman Sachs ( GS ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ). Nasdaq 100 winners included T-Mobile US ( TMUS ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and eBay ( EBAY ).
X The Nasdaq composite led the way, rising 2.7%. The S&P 500 rallied 1.9% and the Dow Jones industrial average gained 1.7%. Small caps lagged a bit with the Russell 2000 up 0.9%. Volume on the Nasdaq was tracking slightly higher than on Tuesday. NYSE volume was lower.
After two days of bullish gains, the Nasdaq is still below its 200-day moving average. Even if it can climb above the 7500 level, the Nasdaq's 50-day moving average around 7778 is another potential resistance level to watch.
Top Stock Gainers: Apple Gaps Up Shares of Apple ( AAPL ) were up 3% ahead of its earnings report Thursday after the close. Its latest pullback has been relatively tame as the stock sits just below its 50-day moving average. Apple was featured as a possible call-option trade, along with Starbucks ( SBUX ), in the latest Earnings Preview column.
Wednesday's session yielded plenty of big movers to the upside, but the outperformance didn't do much to improve the charts.
Among the FAANG stocks , shares of Facebook ( FB ) were up nearly 5% after earnings per share handily beat estimates. Sales growth and monthly active users slightly missed. Wall Street seemed to focus on lower costs, plus Facebook's future plans to monetize assets like Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger.
Meanwhile, General Motors ( GM ) gapped above its 50-day moving average, rising 9% to 36.53, but it's 200-day line around 38 remains a potential resistance level to watch. Earnings and sales topped estimates, helped by strength in China. Full-size trucks and crossover vehicles fueled North America demand.
Inside the IBD 50 , top stock gainers included HealthEquity ( HQY ). It showed bullish technical action with a gap above its 50-day moving average. Trade Desk ( TTD ) also outperformed, rising 8%, but like most other growth stocks, it's technically challenged below the 50-day moving average.
Regional banks outperformed as money flowed out of bonds. That pushed the 10-year Treasury yield higher by 3 basis points to 3.15%. But finding bullish charts in the financial sector isn't an easy task. Among the regional banks, the highest Composite Rating in the group belongs to U.S. Bancorp ( USB ), but it's still stuck below its 50-day moving average after a failed breakout.
